newsitem.title: USA: Nacco says lift-truck sales fell in Q1.
newsitem.headline: Nacco says lift-truck sales fell in Q1.

text.p: Nacco Industries said on Friday its quarterly revenues and net income fell as lift-truck sales by its NACCO Materials Handling Group dropped 25.5 percent.

Nacco Materials Handling Group's first quarter net income was $3.5 million, compared with $12.2 million for the first quarter of 1996. Revenues for the quarter were $332.3 million, compared with $420.8 million for the first quarter of 1996. Nacco's Materials Handling Group sold 14,529 lift trucks worldwide in the first quarter of 1997, down from 19,492 sold in the same period a year ago, the company said.
The company attributed the decrease to weaker retail demand in the Americas, slower sales in some key European ma kets and extremely competitive markets in Asia-Pacific.
Also, unit volumes during the first quarter of 1996 were positively affected by a backlog reduction that did not recur in the first quarter of 1997.

Product pricing had a moderately negative impact on earnings compared with the prior year primarily due to competitive pressures in the Americas. The company said other factors that contributed to the decline were weaker retail demand in the Americas and slower sales in some key European markets.
The company also said the decline in net income was caused by lower manufacturing capacity use due to lower unit volumes in 1997 and a nonrecurring tax benefit in the first quarter of 1996.

The company said net income for the first quarter of 1997 was positively affected by a favorable sales mix of higher margin trucks, higher demand for parts and reduced costs for incentive and profit sharing programs.
